reason: E3 directly supports amorphization and nanobridge toughening in UFG Cantor alloy, but it does not address strain-rate dependence. E1 discusses general toughening mechanisms but provides no evidence for amorphization or its rate sensitivity. The key premise that lower strain rate triggers amorphization is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Deformation-induced crystalline-to-amorphous phase transformation occurs at crack tips in ultrafine-grained CrMnFeCoNi.
Amorphous nanobridges form in the crack wake and shield the crack, enhancing toughness.
Lower strain rates promote this amorphization by allowing atomic mobility and stress relaxation.
Higher strain rates suppress amorphization, leading to dislocation-mediated deformation and lower toughness.
The proposed mechanism is the primary source of toughness variation with strain rate in this alloy.
